tb21_profile.skill: Bounded-concurrency async scheduling plus correct cancellation semantics: a semaphore/TaskGroup limit, and propagating CancelledError/KeyboardInterrupt so every task's cleanup code still runs
tb21_profile.domain: Python asyncio (tasks, gather, semaphores, CancelledError, signal/KeyboardInterrupt handling)
tb21_profile.task_form: implement-a-small-API-from-spec whose difficulty is entirely in subtle concurrency edge cases

TMax-15K.reason: Requires the async function to terminate on cancellation and explicitly forbids catching or swallowing asyncio.CancelledError - the exact semantics here.
Server ignores client cancellation and leaves an orphaned task; fix is to handle asyncio.CancelledError so the task actually stops.
Asyncio task leak when a client goes away - same lifecycle bug the run_tasks contract exists to prevent.
Service leaks asyncio tasks on client disconnect; must make in-flight tasks be cancelled and torn down.
Asyncio task leak causing memory exhaustion, plus a regression test that proves tasks are reclaimed - tests cancellation hygiene.
Vendored async package leaks asyncio tasks and connections when a build aborts; abort-path cleanup is the crux.
Asyncio chunk-processing service leaks memory/tasks; requires reasoning about task lifetime in a running event loop.
Defines the leak precisely as tasks cancelled without their cleanup ever emitted - the exact failure mode, though the work is log analysis.
Must enforce a strict semaphore of at most 4 concurrent calls while fanning work out - the max_concurrent half, in Go.
Concurrent handlers lose updates; fix by making the critical section async-safe with asyncio.Lock - concurrency primitive selection.

Recursive-Task-Synthesis.reason: Two things run concurrently and on SIGINT all children must be terminated cleanly - the interrupt-must-still-clean-up requirement.
Runs until interrupted and must flush collected state to disk before exiting on SIGTERM or KeyboardInterrupt - cleanup on interrupt.
On EOF or SIGINT the script must still print its summary and exit message - finalisation code that survives the interrupt.
Three concurrent background jobs are stopped/resumed/terminated with Unix signals; process-level analogue of cancelling tasks.
Manage concurrent background workers to a spec, including their orderly signalling and shutdown.
Drive a runner whose parallelism is capped by NUMBER_OF_PARALLEL_COMMANDS and which must tolerate individual failures.
Start several concurrent writers and manage their lifecycle with signals; same start-many-then-stop-them-all shape.
Background processes appending to a shared file, controlled by signals; concurrency without any cancellation subtlety.
Build a parallel processing pipeline with a worker pool library - fan-out only, no cancellation or cleanup guarantee.
Run several long processes concurrently, capture their output and then signal them; shell-level process control.

TerminalWorld-Seeds-Clean.reason: Probes what detaching an async task does to its link and liveness - exactly the ownership question behind cancelling and cleaning up tasks.
Monitor a spawned process, kill it, and capture the exit reason delivered to the monitor - forced termination plus its notification.
Implement concurrent fan-out over a list of inputs by spawning async tasks and collecting each result - the non-cancel half of run_tasks.
Concurrent background workers driven through signal handling; a process-level version of interrupting running jobs.
Pause, terminate and resume specific concurrent processes with SIGSTOP/SIGTERM - selective cancellation of running work.
Exercise a runner whose parallelism is capped by an env var and which must not abort the batch when one command fails.
Write a Python script that fans work out across a process pool; concurrency API usage with no cancellation semantics.
Parallel pipeline over 1000 items with a pool library - throughput-style concurrency only.
Drive a Go concurrent process executor over two command sets; running many jobs at once, nothing about stopping them.
Serial vs parallel waiting with timeouts and exit codes; only the wait-for-many-things-at-once idea transfers.

SWE-Smith-Seeds-Clean.reason: bounded_gather is a semaphore-limited asyncio.gather; the bug is in how the concurrency limit is validated - the same function being asked for.
Add shield support to cancel scopes - shielding is precisely how cleanup code is allowed to finish after a cancel.
Signal handling (the Ctrl-C path) plus subprocess pipe setup inside an async runtime - interrupt delivery in a concurrent program.
Async generator finalisation is broken - whether teardown code runs when an async object is discarded, the same guarantee.
Timeout state machine after exit/expiration; async_timeout works by cancelling the task and re-interpreting CancelledError.
Timeout object behaves unexpectedly around its cancellation callbacks; requires reading asyncio cancellation flow carefully.
reject() allows invalid state transitions in a cancellation-driven timeout - state validity across cancel points.
Registration accepts non-coroutine callables where awaitables are required - the Callable[[], Awaitable] contract this API also has.
Sync-to-async wrapper drops the result of the wrapped call; awaiting across the sync/async boundary correctly.
Type sleep_forever as NoReturn; structured-concurrency library domain but the fix is a typing annotation.

SWE-Rebench-Tasks-Clean.reason: Whole issue is when to cancel a future versus set an exception, and how callers can tell why CancelledError arrived - core cancellation design.
Exception structure escaping a nursery when children fail or are cancelled; how errors from concurrent children reach the caller.
Server-side tasks stay alive longer than they should after the peer goes away; deciding when to cancel outstanding work.
Failure inside an await asyncio.gather(*tasks) cleanup path - cleanup that itself awaits, which is what run_tasks must get right.
A cancelled request corrupts later requests; reasoning about state left behind when a coroutine is cancelled mid-flight.
KeyboardInterrupt lands while waiting on a child process and leaves a lock held - Ctrl-C arriving at the worst moment.
Graceful shutdown does not drain as documented; shutting down running handlers in an orderly way.
keepalive_ping's wait_for/timeout interaction misbehaves - timeouts implemented on top of task cancellation.
Two long-running tasks gathered together with signal handling disabled; lifetime and interruption of gathered tasks.
Async client call hangs/fails against a finished pod; asyncio API debugging with no cancellation content.

final_top10.reason: Explicitly requires the coroutine to terminate on cancellation and not swallow asyncio.CancelledError - the same rule this task turns on.
bounded_gather is a semaphore-bounded asyncio.gather; the bug lives in its concurrency-limit handling, exactly run_tasks' signature.
Deep argument about cancelling futures versus raising, and what a task can know when CancelledError arrives.
Orphaned task survives client cancellation; must handle asyncio.CancelledError so the work actually stops.
Shielding a cancel scope is the mechanism that lets cleanup finish after cancellation - the requirement stated in the prompt.
Asyncio task leak when a client disconnects; tasks must be cancelled and reaped rather than left running.
How exceptions from concurrently running children surface out of a nursery - the structured-concurrency version of this API.
On SIGINT every concurrently running child must be terminated cleanly - the keyboard-interrupt-still-cleans-up requirement.
Signal (Ctrl-C) delivery inside an async runtime, the path by which a KeyboardInterrupt becomes a cancellation.
Fix an asyncio task leak on disconnect so abandoned tasks are cancelled instead of accumulating.

notes: Strongest task of the five for retrieval: TMax has a whole family of asyncio cancellation/task-leak tasks and SWE-Smith/Rebench cover trio, async-timeout, websockets and aiohttp cancellation directly, so final_top10 is dominated by those three pools. The two weak corpora are RTS and TerminalWorld: neither contains asyncio at all, so their ten are Unix-signal process-control and pool-parallelism tasks - the SIGINT-cleanup ones (rts_task_d0d85b0aa334978c5f38571f, rts_task_0e6f1cc0fb0e1aef5a9781eb) genuinely teach the cleanup-on-interrupt discipline, but everything below rank 6 in those two lists is fan-out-only and scored 2. The lexical shortlist for RTS/TW was almost pure noise (pipx/Taskwarrior/npm chores that merely mention 'task'); every RTS and TW id above came from my own signal/concurrency searches.
